Manulife is seeking an experienced Manager / Senior Manager, AI Model Risk & Operational Risk Oversight to provide independent second-line oversight and challenge of AI-enabled solutions across the enterprise. This role sits at the intersection of AI, technology, and risk management, helping ensure that AI-related model risks and operational risks are effectively identified, assessed, monitored, and governed. The successful candidate will partner with business, technology, data science, and governance stakeholders to provide credible challenge, influence risk-informed decision-making, and support the responsible adoption of emerging technologies, including Generative AI and Agentic AI. This is a unique opportunity to shape the future of AI risk governance while developing deep expertise in one of the fastest-growing areas of enterprise risk management.
 Position Responsibilities: 
 Provide independent second-line oversight and challenge of AI model risks and operational risks associated with AI-enabled solutions, platforms, and business processes.
 Review and assess medium- and high-risk AI use cases, ensuring risks are appropriately identified, evaluated, mitigated, monitored, and escalated.
 Evaluate AI governance, model risk management practices, operational controls, monitoring programs, incident management activities, and regulatory compliance processes.
 Assess risks associated with machine learning models, Generative AI, large language models, foundation models, third-party AI services, and Agentic AI solutions.
 Review operational resilience, technology risk, third-party risk, change management, access controls, and incident response processes supporting AI solutions.
 Conduct thematic reviews to identify emerging risks, recurring control weaknesses, governance gaps, and systemic issues across AI portfolios.
 Develop and communicate independent risk opinions, oversight assessments, executive reporting, and committee materials.
 Provide effective challenge to business, technology, data science, and governance stakeholders while maintaining clear second-line independence.
 Support the evolution of AI Model Risk Management and Operational Risk Management frameworks, standards, methodologies, and governance practices.
 Monitor emerging industry trends, regulatory developments, and leading practices related to AI, technology risk, and responsible AI.
  Required Qualifications: 
 7+ years of relevant experience for Manager-level candidates or 10+ years for Senior Manager-level candidates.
 Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Artificial Intelligence, Statistics, Mathematics, Engineering, Risk Management, Business, or a related discipline.
 Experience in Operational Risk, Technology Risk, Model Risk Management, Enterprise Risk Management, Internal Audit, Compliance, or related risk functions.
 Experience assessing or overseeing AI, machine learning, advanced analytics, or technology-enabled solutions.
 Strong understanding of risk management frameworks, governance practices, control environments, and regulatory requirements within a regulated industry.
 Demonstrated ability to influence senior stakeholders and provide independent challenge on complex risk matters.
 Strong written, verbal, analytical, and presentation skills.
 Bilingualism (English and French) is a strong asset. If the successful candidate is in Québec, proficiency in both languages will be required to support clients from various provinces outside of Quebec.
  Preferred Qualifications: 
 Experience within financial services, insurance, banking, or another highly regulated industry.
 Knowledge of AI Model Risk Management frameworks and model lifecycle governance practices.
 Familiarity with Generative AI, large language models (LLMs), foundation models, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and Agentic AI solutions.
 Understanding of technology risk, operational resilience, third-party risk, cybersecurity, and AI governance frameworks.
 Practical familiarity with Python, SQL, analytics tools, or machine learning environments.
 Experience developing executive reporting, risk assessments, governance committee materials, or oversight opinions.
 Knowledge of emerging regulatory expectations related to AI, model risk, operational risk, or technology risk management.

Hi! 👋 I'm Chris https://www.linkedin.com/in/chkrlee/, head of Product Design at Ashby.

We're looking for a versatile, intrinsically motivated designer who is excited to contribute to rethinking how modern software is designed. At Ashby, you'll be part designer, part product manager, part consultant, and part design system manager (or some combination of the 4!). We do design differently here, and if that excites you, read on.

Our unique approach is working - we're growing >100% year-over-year and have notable customers like Notion, Linear, Shopify, and Snowflake. Our growth and retention metrics are best-in-class among our peers: we have tens of millions in ARR, very low churn, and many years of runway. We're backed by amazing investors like Y Combinator, Elad Gil, Lachy Groom, and many more! We’ll share more details once we meet.




HOW WE WORK

In my previous roles, product teams always consisted of a product manager, a designer, and ~4-5 engineers. This may sound familiar to you! The product manager briefs the designer who then designs. After designing, mocks are handed to the engineers. 

We take a more principled approach here at Ashby. If you've been designing software enough, you'll realize in actuality, design is required in varying degrees on each project. Sometimes in the past, I'd be asked to design yet another settings page, when really all that was needed was an engineer to reuse existing components and just follow some documentation I had written. Other times, I felt I should effectively be the product manager and own a project from beginning to end. In these latter cases, it made sense that I was even the one providing project updates and managing resources rather than constantly being pinged by a separate product manager.

This principled approach is now what we do here, and it is part of what has allowed Ashby to take down incumbents in multiple verticals all at once. We don't settle for the status quo—we actively resist reversion to the mean.

Currently, I report to Benji, the co-founder & CEO. Both Abhik and Benji (our founders) care deeply about design, which at first glance may seem counterintuitive given the number of full-time designers that we employ. The belief is not that design is unimportant, but rather that it should be owned by the product team collectively, not solely by a group of full-time designers who happen to have the job title. 

The design department’s job at Ashby is not to make every single design decision but to equip our entire product team to make better decisions themselves, as well as edit decisions that PMs/Engineers choose to make. That, while tackling the biggest design challenges ourselves. 



Separate from design, you may also be excited by the fact that we maintain a near seed-stage-like culture with fuzzy lines between functional roles, as much autonomy as you can handle, and a focus on IC-work with an almost-no-meeting culture. While you get the product-market fit and scale of a growth-stage startup, you also get the agency and no-nonsense, no-red-tape culture of a seed-stage startup.




WHAT WE’RE BUILDING

Talent teams aspire to build a hiring process that identifies great candidates, moves them quickly through the interview process, and provides an excellent experience for the candidate. To accomplish this, recruiters perform thousands of daily tasks to coordinate and relay information between candidates, interviewers, and hiring managers. Teams struggle to keep up!



Scheduling a final round is an excellent example of our customers' challenges. A recruiter needs to collect availability from the candidate, identify potential interviewers, perform “Calendar Tetris” to find who is available to interview the candidate, schedule on the earliest date possible, and perform any last-minute adjustments as availability changes. They must perform this while considering the interview load on each individual and whether interviewers need to be trained and shadowing others. 



Ashby provides talent teams with intelligent and powerful software that provides insights into where they’re failing and automates or simplifies many of the tasks they’re underwater with. We put a lot of effort into designing products that are approachable to beginners but mastered and extended by power users. In many ways, spreadsheets set the bar here (and are what we often replace!).




WHY YOU SHOULD OR SHOULDN’T APPLY




YOUR QUALIFICATIONS:

 - 4+ years of product design experience in desktop SaaS.

 - Able to think from first principles instead of simply applying the “standard” UX processes.

 - Can break down complex user problems by asking questions that narrow down the solution space.

 - Enough experience that your intuition can solve many usability problems without having to rely solely on data & metrics or conducting user research.

 - Curious & resourceful enough to come up with creative solutions and de-risk them appropriately.

 - Strong skills in layout, navigation, IA, UI, and interaction design.

 - Strong visual design skills and obsession with craft & details.

 - As a bonus, you have experience at an early-stage startup or have spent time as a solo designer on a team.




YOU MAY WANT TO APPLY IF YOU’RE EXCITED ABOUT:

 - Creating leverage and impact far and above what you'd see in a typical EPD product team structure. You won’t be a cog in the wheel, the wheel is not very big!

 - Getting to work on all parts of a massive product surface area - spanning many user types, JTBDs, usability challenges, etc. Unlike in other organizations, you won’t be stuck working on one problem for many years.

 - Helping reinvent the design model for modern enterprise software—you don’t have to build wireframes, user journeys, personas, etc. What matters is solving a customer’s problem; what tools you use are up to you.

 - Covering all parts of the design process with a focus on design craft. You'll still be doing the occasional user research interview but will be focused on using heuristics & experience to improve our IA, navigation, interactions, UI patterns, and more.

 - Helping build our design system from (almost) the ground up.


CONVERSELY, YOU MAY NOT WANT TO APPLY IF:

 - You feel uncomfortable designing independently without much guidance from a PM or design management.

 - You’re uncomfortable having your decisions and process being challenged constantly by engineering & product.

 - You prefer an in-person role over remote (Ashby operates remotely).

 - You dislike written documentation.

 - You want a set structure and rhythm to your projects.
   
   - PM gives you a brief, you do wireframes, then mocks, then pass off work to engineers. Rinse and repeat.

 - You prefer a narrow job scope - interaction design only, design system only, etc.


ON A WEEKLY BASIS YOU WILL FIND YOURSELF:

 - Consulting for engineers who need help structuring layout, typography, flows, etc.

 - Digging into problems by consulting GTM, talking to customers, asking for data requests, and more in order to present confident assumptions about your proposals.

 - Using Figma to draw out your ideas and create visual artifacts for stakeholder alignment.

 - Writing specification docs (we call them specs!) that detail your design proposals. These documents are meant to get stakeholder alignment on the biggest decisions you want to make and are a core part of how we work at Ashby.

 - Taking ownership of larger product features and thinking through Jobs-To-Be-Done, navigation, information architecture, layout, interaction, etc.

 - Taking in customer feedback and using heuristics to build your own usability backlog and propose projects for engineers to take on.

 - Consolidating and refining our design system to be functional, aesthetic, and best-in-class.


INTERVIEW PROCESS

At Ashby, our team and interview process want to help you show your best self. We’ll dive into past projects and simulate working together and talking through decisions. Our interview process is four rounds with some casual Zoom coffee in between to get to know each other: 

 1. 30m introduction call to discuss Ashby and your experience

 2. 45m portfolio review

 3. 75m design exercise and app teardown. The exercise will be a live whiteboarding exercise where we provide a prompt and you show us how you'd break down problems and come up with solutions. 

 4. 2.5hr final round - meet the team + portfolio repeat with a founder

I'll be your main point of contact and prepare you for interviews. You’ll meet other engineers and product managers as well (with lots of time to ask them questions). If we don’t give an offer by the last round, I'll provide feedback as to why if you'd like it (I'm serious!).




BENEFITS

 - Competitive salary and equity.

 - 10-year exercise window for stock options. You shouldn’t feel pressure to purchase stock options if you leave Ashby —do it when you feel financially comfortable. This is one of the reasons I joined personally - not a lot of startups do this.

 - Unlimited PTO with four weeks recommended per year. Expect “Vacation?” in our one-on-one agenda until you start taking it.

 - Twelve weeks of fully paid family leave in the US. We plan to expand this to employees in other countries as situations arise.

 - Generous equipment, software, and office furniture budget. Get what you need to be happy and productive!

 - $100/month education budget with more expensive items (like conferences) covered with manager approval.

 - If you’re in the US, top-notch health insurance for you and your dependents with all premiums covered by us.

Ashby’s success hinges on hiring great people and creating an environment where we can be happy, feel challenged, and do our best work. We’re being deliberate about building that environment from the ground up. I hope that excites you enough to apply.

Ashby provides equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, genetics, sexual orientation, gender identity, or gender expression. We are committed to a diverse and inclusive workforce and welcome people from all backgrounds, experiences, perspectives, and abilities.

Ashby is committed to a fair and transparent hiring process. We confirm that this advertisement is for an active, existing vacancy within our organization. Please be advised that we may use artificial intelligence-driven tools to assist our recruitment team in screening, assessing, and selecting candidates for this position.

Reporting to a Supervisor, Hamilton Paramedic Service, the paramedic provides primary emergency medical care and transportation for ill and/or injured persons in the community to, from, and between treatment facilities, in specially equipped ambulance vehicles and emergency response vehicles.  GENERAL DUTIES 
Provide primary emergency medical care for ill and/or injured persons at the emergency site by providing basic and advanced pre-hospital life support.
Provide transportation for ill and/or injured persons, to, from, and between treatment facilities, in specially equipped ambulance vehicles as directed by the dispatching Central Ambulance Communications Centre (CACC).
 Deliver thorough patient assessment and treatment in accordance to Provincial and local standards and medical directives.
Responsible for all medical interventions as deemed essential by the Base Hospital and Hamilton Paramedic Service, including: controlled drug therapy, manual defibrillation, and cardiac dysrhythmia interpretation according to Provincial Medical Directives.

Inspect, restock, and maintain ambulance stations in a clean and operational state.
Completion of all required documentation, including but not limited to Ambulance Call Reports, Incident/Occurrence Reports, Logistics Reports, Vehicle Inspection Reports, and any other report as deemed necessary by the Hamilton Paramedic Service and/or the Ministry of Health and Long-Term Care.
Participate in Continuing Education as required and participate in the training/precepting of Advanced Care and Primary Care paramedic students and other allied healthcare professionals.

About Portless 
 Portless helps fast-growing direct-to-consumer brands ship orders from our fulfillment centers in China straight to their customers in North America, the UK and beyond. Brands no longer have to import and warehouse inventory in every market, which frees up cash and cuts costs. 
 We run the whole chain: fulfillment, freight, customs clearance and last-mile delivery, tied together by our own software and AI. Our merchants are mid-market brands in apparel, beauty, electronics and home goods. 
 We are venture-backed and on track to double revenue in 2026. Our team works across North America, China and beyond. 
 You will own Portless's books end to end: the monthly close across our entities in North America and Asia, merchant billing and collections, cash, and our first external audit. You will lead our accounting team, most of whom are based in China, and build the processes and controls that let us keep growing fast. 
 This is a hands-on role. You will be in the reconciliations yourself before you hand them off, and you will have real ownership from day one. 
 What you'll own 
 Month-end close. Own the close calendar across all entities, including consolidation, intercompany and FX, and get it done faster each month. 
 Billing and order-to-cash. Make sure every merchant is billed correctly and on time. That includes rate-card changes, credit notes and waivers with clear approvals, duties, VAT and tariffs billed back accurately, and cash applied across Stripe and our other payment channels. 
 AR and collections. Keep AR reconciled to the bank and payment processors, set our bad-debt reserve policy, and run collections with our billing team. 
 Cash. Own the daily cash position and a 13-week forecast tied to the bank, plus payment runs and approvals. 
 Audit and diligence. Select and lead our first external audit, prepare the books for investor and lender diligence, and own monthly lender reporting. 
 Tax and compliance. Coordinate outside advisors on Canadian, US and Chinese filings, sales tax and VAT, and transfer pricing. 
 Systems and controls. Tighten our stack (QuickBooks Online, Stripe, Bill.com, Ramp), document how things get done, and decide when we need an ERP. 
 Team. Lead and develop the accounting team, give every process a clear owner, and work closely with our data and engineering teams on billing data. 
 What success looks like in your first year 
 Outcome 
 By 
 90 days 
 You own the daily cash position and monthly lender reporting, and the whole team works from one close calendar. 
 6 months 
 Every entity closes by business day 10, and every rate-card change, credit note and waiver has an approval trail. 
 12 months 
 Our first external audit is complete. AR ties to the bank and payment processors every month, and duties and VAT billed match what we paid. The team runs on documented processes. 
 What you bring 
 CPA, CA or an equivalent designation. 
 8+ years in accounting, including at least 3 as a controller or assistant controller who owned the close. 
 A start in audit at a Big 4 or mid-tier public accounting firm. 
 You have owned a multi-entity, multi-currency close, including consolidation and intercompany.

We’re looking for an Associate Editor to help us give our readers the best and most jam-packed money know-how that can be found anywhere in the country ‒ in bite-sized stories Canadians actually look forward to reading. 
 Think you can deliver?
 Who we are
 moneyGenius is a proudly Atlantic Canadian company with a simple mission: 
 Make money easy and fun for everyone. 
 To achieve this, we’re committed to making both moneyGenius.ca and creditcardGenius.ca the leading Canadian resources for all things money. In addition, we're reinventing personal finance education and rewards with our new GeniusCash app that makes learning about and maximizing your money fun and engaging.
 Our team helps over 400K Canadians per month make the most informed financial decisions by building best-in-class fintech products and crafting high-quality educational content. Through GeniusCash rewards, Canadians have banked over $6.4M since 2021.
 And if that wasn’t enough, we were named one of Canada’s Top Growing Companies and Top Growing Women-Led Companies by The Globe and Mail's Report on Business Magazine, as well as a winner in Deloitte’s Technology Fast 50 program. These achievements are a testament to our growth, and reflect the remarkable hard work, dedication, and unwavering commitment of our team to our mission: to make money easy and fun for all Canadians. 
 So if you want in on our mission, read on…
 What you'll do
 We need an organized, detail-oriented Associate Editor who can write well-researched finance-focused stories, sharpen good content into something remarkable, manage our increasingly fast-paced editorial calendar, and keep things moving from idea to publication. In this role, you will:
 Manage a daily short-form content calendar, keeping topics and deadlines on track
 Brief content topics, with clear direction on audience, angle, and user experience
 Write well-researched personal finance content
 Edit content, polishing good work until every word tells and it's ready to publish
 Fact-check every piece for accuracy before it goes live
 Review all content through a reader's eye, making sure it flows as a cohesive whole and every link works
 Shape every story for a fun and memorable mobile app experience
 Refine editorial practices regularly, adapting to results like user engagement data
 Make sure every piece meets our Editorial Style Guide and quality standards
 Manage each piece of content end to end, following up until every task is closed
 Support stretch projects and cross-functional work as needed
 What it's really like working here
 We believe in being transparent about what this role entails – both the exciting parts and the challenges.
 You'll wear many hats in a lean startup environment . As a bootstrapped company, we don't have layers of specialized staff. Some days you'll be writing content from scratch; other days you'll be editing, fact-checking, planning the editorial calendar, or repurposing existing content. If you thrive on variety and get energized by tackling different challenges, you'll love it here. If you prefer a highly specialized role with a narrow set of responsibilities, this might not be the right fit.
 Quality and consistency are non-negotiable . We're a process-driven company because that's our competitive advantage. You'll need to follow our Editorial Style Guide and documented processes, and maintain meticulous attention to detail. We don't reinvent the wheel on recurring tasks – we perfect the process once and apply it consistently.
 We embrace experimentation and innovation . While we rely on our processes for repeat tasks, we also take on new challenges and are always evolving to respond to a changing content landscape. You’ll need to be ready to try new tools, measure your results, and adapt.
 Responsiveness matters deeply . We expect responses within hours on Zoom and within a business day by email. You'll need to close every communication loop by confirming completion or passing the ball to the next person. 
 Accountability is how we grow . When something goes wrong, we don't point fingers. We ask what we could have done differently and how we can capture those lessons into our processes. You'll be expected to take ownership of your work, proactively communicate when you need help, and deliver what you promised when you promised it.
 Fast-paced means really fast-paced . We're a lean team executing ambitious projects. Some weeks will be intense. You'll need to juggle multiple deadlines, think on your feet, and occasionally put in extra effort to get content out the door.
 The work matters . You're not just filling a content calendar – you're helping Canadians make better financial decisions. Your accuracy and high standards directly impact the trust our readers place in our brand.
 What makes it worth it
 You'll have real impact . In a small team, your contributions are visible and meaningful. You're not a cog in a machine – you're an essential part of making our mission happen.
 You'll grow fast . The variety of challenges and our commitment to evolution means you'll develop skills quickly, from writing and editing to managing custom content tools. We invest in our people because our success depends on your success.
 You'll work with people who care . Everyone here is committed to excellence and genuinely supports each other. We're building something meaningful together, and that creates a special team dynamic.
 Who you are
 You have 1 – 3 years of experience in writing, editing, or content management, ideally in a fast-paced startup or digital publishing setting.
 You have a bachelor's degree in Business, Journalism, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
 You're legally eligible to work in Canada.
 You've got a passion for learning, fine-tuned attention to detail, and consistently high standards.
 You bring a strong work ethic and thrive in a demanding startup environment.
 Nothing slips by you with your organizational and time management skills.
 You prioritize your tasks with urgency and deadlines in mind and have impeccable follow-through.
 You've got a bias for action – you love checking things off your to-do list and getting things done.
 You write clearly and persuasively, with a sharp eye for accuracy, structure, and tone.
 You're comfortable with tools like Google Workspace and content management systems.
 You’re ready to leverage AI tools for productivity without offloading your creativity or accountability.
 You thrive in a remote-first environment and know how to stay connected and productive while working from home.
 You're able to work in ET or AT time zones because most of our team is located in Eastern and Atlantic Canada, making overlapping work hours essential for real-time collaboration and timely communication.
 You have a growth mindset – you're always learning, adapting, and ready to take on new challenges.
 Being well-versed in money in several of the following areas would be ideal:
 Cars and transportation – Getting from point A to point B is expensive and something we all need to do. Buying and selling cars, car maintenance, car sharing, commuting, public transit, parking, taxis, etc.
 Credit cards – Points, welcome bonuses, rate-of-return calculations, churning, credit score, perks, insurance, fraud, acceptance, low interest balance transfers, risks, etc.
 Entertainment – Dining out, attractions, movies, music, adventures, outdoor activities, games, etc.
 Finances – Banking, saving, investing, budgeting, personal finance, money-saving strategies, loans, etc.
 Food and groceries – We all need to eat, so everyone wants to save on food. Couponing, flyers, sales, rewards, price matching, buying local, buying bulk, wholesalers, gardening, freezer cooking, buying in season, etc.
 Housing – Having a roof over our heads is necessary and expensive. Buying and selling real estate, rent, heating and cooling, maintenance, landscaping, yard work, furnishings, property taxes, etc.
 Increasing income – Salary negotiation, starting a side hustle, etc.
 Insurance – Car, home, life, disability, rental, credit card, etc.
 Investing – RRSPs, TFSAs, ETFs, mutual funds, DIY investing, diversification, etc.
 Rewards programs – Retail and travel rewards programs within Canada and internationally
 Services – Home phone, cell phones, TV/cable/satellite, internet, etc.
 Taxes – Basically any way you can lessen your tax burden legally. Tax credits, income splitting, income deferral, tax software, tax strategies, etc.
 Travel – Flights, trains, car rentals, hotels, resorts, cruises, currency conversion, etc.
 This role is perfect for you if you:
 Take pride in doing things right, not just getting them done
 Can juggle multiple deadlines without dropping balls
 Know how to make educational content fun and interesting
 Enjoy making good writing even better
 Communicate clearly and follow through consistently
 Value accuracy, efficiency, and continuous improvement
 See style guides and documented processes as helpful structure, not bureaucracy
 Get energized by refining systems and making them better over time
 This role is NOT right for you if you:
 Prefer only writing, or only editing, with a narrow focus
 Need step-by-step direction for every task or struggle with self-motivation
 Get frustrated by fast-changing priorities
 See style guides and editorial feedback as red tape rather than a competitive advantage
 Want a traditional 9–5 with clear work-life boundaries every week
 What you'll get
 We take care of our team. Here's a quick list of benefits you'll get working with us:
 Work from home anywhere in Canada with permanent remote full-time status
 Opportunities for continuous growth and career advancement
 Competitive salary based on your skills and experience
 Performance-based bonuses
 100% paid premiums for health, dental, and vision insurance
 Ample vacation time and standardized public holidays across Canada
 New employee toolkit that contains everything you need to do your job well (includes a company laptop, a second monitor, and a dozen other useful items)
 Mental health support through inConfidence and the Calm app
 Mobile phone allowance to help cover part of your monthly bill
 Regular team-building fun including team games, lunches, happy hours, competitions with prizes, and more
 Challenging and rewarding work that has a real impact on the financial health of Canadians
 Let's talk
 Please apply with your cover letter addressed to Tanya so we know that you thoughtfully reviewed our job description.
